error_note: A virus-specific complement-fixation titer is not a measure of total immunoglobulin concentration; a high echovirus 7 titer has no bearing on mu-heavy chain disease.

Hypoglycemia in holoprosencephaly (via pituitary deficiency) is an uncommon, nonspecific feature shared by about 200 diseases, and a low value 5 hours into a 100 g tolerance test reflects reactive hypoglycemia rather than the fasting hypoglycemia annotated.

Post-load hyperglycemia is characteristic of Rabson-Mendenhall syndrome, but the hypoglycemia of the disease is fasting, so a low value 45 minutes after a glucose dose is not how it is shown, and high at 45 minutes needs its own criteria.
A lupus anticoagulant screen/confirm ratio is a coagulation test, a low ratio is the normal result, and the near-root immune-physiology bridge gives no real link to this hypopigmentation syndrome.

ANA positivity is a variable, nonspecific finding in proteasome-associated autoinflammatory syndromes; the obligate frequency rests on very few reported patients and the test is not used to recognise the disease.
A blunted LH response fits the hypogonadotropic hypogonadism of X-linked AHC, but the code leaves the challenge agent unspecified, so what counts as a low 1-hour value is undefined.
The CSF lactate elevation of mitochondrial/copper-transport disease is L-lactate; D-lactate is a bacterial metabolite measured for suspected bacterial meningitis and is a different analyte.
A low farmer's-lung precipitin IgG is a normal finding with no pathological reading, bridged through a near-root metabolism term to a disease it has nothing to do with.
Detecting desipramine shows a xenobiotic in serum, but a low (subtherapeutic or undetectable) level does not indicate that, and the term says nothing about the high/toxic reading the result carries.
C-peptide in KATP hyperinsulinism is inappropriately unsuppressed relative to glucose rather than absolutely high, and an eighth serial specimen of an unspecified series has no defined high.
A low allergen-specific IgE is the normal, non-sensitised result and says nothing about total circulating immunoglobulin concentration.
Hepatitis E IgG is an antibody test, not a viremia measure, and the generic viremia bridge loses the pathogen: HEV serology has no bearing on yellow fever.

Suppressed C-peptide occurs only in the rare IGF2-mediated hypoglycemia of solitary fibrous tumor and is shown during spontaneous hypoglycemia; a low value 5 minutes after glucose reflects a poor insulin response, not that state.

The disease record lists abnormal CSF morphology as explicitly not a feature of hereditary spastic paraplegia 37, yet a positive association was emitted, in both directions and through a very general term.
Hyperglycemia is recorded at 0% (excluded) for this disease, and a glucose rise after lactose is the normal lactose-tolerance response rather than hyperglycemia.
3-Methylhistidine is a marker of muscle protein breakdown and meat intake, a different analyte from histidine; its elevation is not hyperhistidinemia.
The source lists hyperglycemia as explicitly not a feature of SH2B1 deficiency, and glucose 15 minutes after a lactose load measures lactase activity, not glycemic status.
Hypoglycemia is a very rare, nonspecific feature of congenital syphilis in sick neonates, and a 90-minute adult 75 g tolerance-test value is not how it would be found.
Diagnosis rests on the shape of the whole audiogram (high-frequency sloping loss, both ears); a single 1000 Hz threshold in one ear is one narrow component and is often near normal early in DFNA2A.
In a lactose tolerance test a glucose rise is the expected normal response and is judged as an increment over baseline, so a high timed value is not simply hyperglycemia.
A low anti-GM1 IgM is the normal result and has no pathological meaning; the near-root immune-physiology term adds nothing.
The mix contains kiwi, tomato and sesame besides the two nuts, so a high result cannot be attributed to nut-specific IgE.

Reduced fragility does mean increased osmotic resistance, but at 0.65% NaCl normal red cells show essentially no lysis, so a low result at this single concentration cannot demonstrate it; resistance is read at lower saline concentrations.
Raised 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D is right for infantile hypercalcemia, but the code is a LOINC Part (the analyte only), not an orderable test with a specimen and property.
An HIV-2 antibody test establishes HIV-2 infection only; AIDS is a stage defined by CD4 count or defining illness, which this test cannot show.

The below-treatment-target bands (up to 15.8 pmol/L on Cobas) are not reference limits: a value such as 14 pmol/L is under target for a treated child yet within the normal range, so it is not a decreased free T4.

MELD is a mortality-risk score for patients already known to have advanced liver disease; a high score can be driven by creatinine or an anticoagulant-raised INR and does not by itself establish hepatic failure.
A low free T4 alone does not establish hypothyroidism: it also occurs in non-thyroidal illness and with assay or drug interference, and TSH is needed; the test shows only decreased free T4.

The CTCAE grade 1 band is given as 0.8 and above with no upper bound (it should end at the lower reference limit), so normal and high lymphocyte counts would fall in a band said to indicate a decreased count.
NYHA class II-III records limitation by any of fatigue, palpitation, dyspnea or angina, so it does not specifically show exertional dyspnea; class is an ordinal grade coded as a POSITIVE result.
